| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | in-progress | 2026-08-12 — library-acquire-and-subscription moved to done — the read side landed as one OpenSpec change: D14's scalar flip (materialize reads the authored version!, checks major agreement against the key's suffix mirroring the target schema's _majorAgrees, pulls exactly that build; filter.go and filter_test.go deleted entire, the Masterminds/semver import left materialize, decodeFilter gone; enumeration survives unexported as a lazy failure diagnostic only — the happy path makes one registry operation per subscription and a missing named build reports the published list scoped to the key's major), D11/D9's identity verification at both library read sites via the new oerrors.IdentityError (module acquire returns it bare from the shared LoadModulePackageWithSource path so Kernel.AcquireModuleFromRegistry and every frontend inherit one implementation; catalog materialize wraps it in MaterializeError Kind catalog, errors.As-reachable), synth's lockstep move (SubscriptionSpec is {Enable, Version-required}, FilterSpec and writeFilter deleted, empty Version refused at synthesis naming the subscription path before any schema fetch), the cache-key trim (normSub drops range/allow/deny; a golden test pins v2 keys byte-identical across the trim), and D41's residue (#moduleInstanceMetadata.fqn now carries the instance's own metadata.fqn via new InstanceMetadata.FQN + InstanceView.InstanceFQN; Version stays, fed by the now-acquire-verified declared version). Transitional scaffolding retired: cue:catalog:drift shrank from the highestStable shell mirror to a named-tag-exists check, opm_platform's pin comment now reads load-bearing/ordinary-update, the materialize_test NOTE tombstone and the synth filter-rejection transitional test are resolved, and the happy-path assertion flipped from coincidence to contract (a HIGHER version is published beside the authored pin and must not be chosen). Everything green: task check, task cue:check against GHCR, forced flow tests (OPM_FLOW_TEST_FORCE=1) materializing catalogs/opm 2.0.0-alpha.3 by its authored version. THREE RECORDED DEVIATIONS. (1) D11's third read point — verify when a catalog is added to a platform's registry — has no library home: the platform loader deliberately resolves no subscriptions, so in-library the check collapses into materialize, and the fires-earliest, platform-author-facing property is delivered by frontends materializing at subscription time (option 1's exported VerifySubscriptions stays available later, deferral free per Principle VII). (2) The opm-operator CRD carries Subscription.Filter — a versioned API field whose retirement is operator-side work, contradicting this entry's 'no operator feature code at all' note in config.yaml affects; operator-library-retarget inherits it. (3) Found at implementation: the acquire-site path clause cannot be unconditional full-path string equality — a core-v0/v1 module's metadata.modulePath is the major-free PARENT path (the 0003 publishing convention; the v0/v1 schema cannot express the suffixed form), and the untouched registry-module-loading spec scenario plus the pinned core-v1 regression fixtures (library#31) keep that read path supported — so the check dispatches on the declared shape: suffixed declarations compare strictly per the design, major-free declarations verify the fetched path sits directly under the declared parent; both shapes still refuse lying metadata, and the version clause is line-independent. DOWNSTREAM HEADS-UP for cli-coordinate-adoption: cli/internal/platform's wireFilter -> synth.FilterSpec mapping no longer compiles and moves to Version, and cli/internal/config/templates.go's template shape moves filter: range: to version: in the same slice. | [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
